description: Shared Renovate preset for digitalnsw repos. Consumer repos extend this via the synced renovate.json (source: repo-files/renovate.json). Edit HERE; Renovate reads it from main at run time, so changes apply everywhere without a sync.

rebaseWhen is pinned to 'conflicted' rather than left at its 'auto' default, because 'auto' silently becomes 'behind-base-branch' on any repo whose branch protection requires branches to be up to date before merging — which is every consumer repo (the Protect main ruleset sets strict_required_status_checks_policy: true, see ONBOARDING.md). Under that default every merge to main rebases EVERY open Renovate PR in the repo, and each rebase re-triggers the full check suite: install, lint, typecheck, format, test, commitlint, ai-pr-title. With prConcurrentLimit 5 that is up to 5 full re-runs per repo per merge, none of which gates the merge that triggered them — the cost is quadratic in merge count, and GitHub bills each job rounded up to the nearest minute. 'conflicted' rebases only when the branch genuinely conflicts (a real lockfile collision Renovate must resolve), so CI runs once per PR you actually merge instead of once per PR per unrelated merge. The trade-off is deliberate: a PR that has fallen behind main now needs an explicit 'Update branch' before it can merge, which spends those minutes at merge time on the one PR that needs them. Revisit if strict_required_status_checks_policy is ever turned off, at which point 'auto' becomes harmless.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security alerting/fix PRs stay with Snyk — avoids duplicate PRs for the same CVE.

schedule: before 7am on the first day of the month
lockFileMaintenance.description: Monthly full lockfile regeneration with real npm — keeps lockfiles fresh and valid. Automerged: the PR touches package-lock.json only, no manifest and no source, and install / install is exactly the gate that proves a regenerated lockfile is coherent — if it passes there is nothing for a human to add by reading a 4000-line lockfile diff. Automerge can never merge a red PR: a regeneration that produces a lockfile npm ci will not install fails install / install and sits open to be closed by hand, exactly as it would have without automerge. rebaseWhen is overridden to behind-base-branch here for the same reason as the dev-patch rule below: the top-level 'conflicted' would strand an automerge PR that falls behind main, because strict required status checks block the merge and nothing would ever refresh the branch.

packageRules.description: npm majors are blocked everywhere they appear (engines, overrides, devDependencies) until the platform bundles the new major. engine-strict=true means pulling in npm ahead of the Vercel/CI bundled npm fails every install with EBADENGINE (see nswds-email#460 — npm 12 needs Node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0, expected bundled with Node 26 ~Oct 2026). Remove this rule as part of the coordinated adoption pass (reusable-ci + engines.node floor + lockfile regen, same shape as nswds-email#458).

Renovate updates to override-pinned packages are disabled at every update type, because two independent failure modes both end in a lockfile that fails npm ci fleet-wide. (1) In-range lockfile-only bumps: Renovate applies them via `npm install <pkg>@<version>`, which adds the package as a direct dependency whose spec conflicts with the override, so npm aborts with EOVERRIDE and the whole grouped PR ships a stale lockfile (nswds-email#459, fast-uri). (2) Range bumps: Renovate rewrites package.json but only half-applies the lockfile — it removes the outgoing entry and never adds the resolved one — so npm ci dies with EUSAGE `Missing: <pkg>@<version> from lock file`. This one is the more dangerous of the two: Renovate posts no artifact-update warning, so the PR looks healthy, and the checks that stay green (Vercel runs `npm install`, which silently repairs it) read as evidence that it isn't (nswds-email#485, postcss-selector-parser ^6.1.3 → ^7.0.0, which took out install, lint, commitlint and editorial). Scoped pins are covered too — Renovate's extractOverrideDepsRec sets depType `overrides` at every nesting level, so `{"@tailwindcss/typography": {"postcss-selector-parser": "^7.0.0"}}` matches this rule. What is given up: the pinned ranges no longer get automatic bump PRs. Monthly lockFileMaintenance still refreshes the resolved version inside each range, and the ranges themselves are vulnerability pins that Snyk already owns (vulnerabilityAlerts is disabled for the same reason) — so raise them by hand off a Snyk finding, the way nswds-email#484 was. Remove this rule when Renovate's npm manager writes correct lockfiles for overrides.

conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits v10 is blocked: preset v10's render-function templates are incompatible with @semantic-release/release-notes-generator@14 — commit analysis still computes correct release types, but generateNotes silently emits an empty changelog body (reproduced with the shared release.config.mjs; tracked upstream as issue #992). v10 also arrives transitively: @commitlint/config-conventional 21.2.0 bumped its ccc dependency from ^9.2.0 to ^10.0.0 and the hoisted copy is what the preset loader finds — this blanked nswds-email changelogs 1.140.5–1.140.12 (nswds-email#437) and, until the 2026-07-19 fleet rollout, every release of nswds-devops and digitalnsw (whose direct pin was on the wrong major, ^10.2.0) plus the newest releases of data, nswds-signature, nswds-community and nswds-email-issues. The fleet carries a direct ^9.3.1 devDependency pin at each repo ROOT — the root hoist resolves v9 for the preset loader while commitlint nests its own v10 — and this rule stops Renovate from majoring those pins back to v10. The pin must be at the root: nswds-ui declared ^9.3.1 in a workspace package and still shipped blank notes for 4.1.4-4.3.0, because semantic-release runs from the root and the preset loader found the hoisted v10 while the workspace copy sat nested. Do NOT treat this rule's text as evidence that the fleet is compliant — an earlier revision asserted all 16 repos were pinned, which was untrue when written (nswds-ui was missing) and went stale as the fleet grew to 27 semantic-release repos; that claim is likely why the gap survived three weeks unexamined. share, created 2026-07-31 after the 2026-07-19 rollout, was never in its scope and shipped a blank v1.0.0. Compliance is now measured, not asserted: ccc-pin-drift-canary.yml scans every repo weekly and opens a tracking issue on drift. When a release-notes-generator release compatible with ccc v10 ships, remove this rule and bump every pin together — take the repo list from the canary, not from this description.

typescript majors (6/7) are blocked: the typescript@7 npm package is the native Go compiler and require('typescript') exposes no JS compiler API, so `next build` fails (Next 16.2.x: 'required package(s) not installed', broke CI and Vercel deploy), eslint crashes via @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree (peer range >=4.8.4 <6.1.0), and prettier-plugin-organize-imports silently no-ops — imports stop being sorted while format hooks keep passing (see nswds-email#444; reproduced 2026-07-18). Native `tsc -b` itself works. Remove when Next.js and typescript-eslint declare TS 6/7 support.

eslint + @eslint/js majors are blocked, and the two MUST move in lockstep: @eslint/js@10 declares peerDependencies { eslint: ^10.0.0 } (v9 declared none), so bumping @eslint/js alone leaves eslint at ^9 and yields an unsatisfiable graph — Renovate cannot regenerate the lockfile (ERESOLVE) and every npm ci fails (EUSAGE). This matcher previously listed only "eslint", which let the eslint-monorepo group split the pair and broke nswds-tokens#132 (superseded by the combined bump in nswds-tokens#140). The block itself stays because ESLint 10 removed context.getFilename(), which eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5 (pulled in transitively by eslint-config-next, incl. 16.2.11) still calls in its React-version detection path — every eslint invocation then crashes with a TypeError before linting a single file (reproduced on nswds-app#418 and locally against eslint-config-next@16.2.11 + eslint@10; upstream jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-react#3977, vercel/next.js#89764). STATUS 2026-07-29: the fixupConfigRules shim ships inside @nswds/eslint-config, the 14 Next.js repos run eslint ^10 through it, and the shared CI lint gate now runs on every PR — the original unblock condition is met for config-next consumers. The block stays for one remaining reason: nswds-ui's workspace eslint-config imports eslint-plugin-react directly with no shim, so an eslint major there would crash its required lint check. Remove this rule once nswds-ui wraps its presets or adopts @nswds/eslint-config/base, and re-check the capped peers (eslint-plugin-import, eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y) at the same time — re-check by 2026-10.

@maizzle/framework and tailwindcss majors are blocked in the two Maizzle 5 repos (nswds-email-framework, nswds-email-starter). Tailwind 4 is incompatible there and the two packages cannot move independently. @maizzle/framework@5.5.0 declares dependencies { tailwindcss: ^3.4.16 }, and tailwindcss-preset-email@1.4.1 -> tailwindcss-email-variants@3.0.5 declares dependencies { tailwindcss: '>=3.4.0 < 4' } — an explicit v4 exclusion. Renovate proposes v4 anyway because the only Tailwind range visible at the top level is tailwindcss-preset-email's PEER of '>=3.4.17', which is unbounded upward; the real ceiling sits one level deeper in a transitive dependency. Merging the v4 bump would not error at install time: npm would put v4 at the root and nest v3 under the packages requiring <4, so tailwind.config.js's `require('tailwindcss/plugin')` — resolved from the project root — would load v4 while the preset chain kept using v3, and Tailwind 4's CSS-first plugin/config model breaks the v3 preset. Tailwind 4 in these repos is gated behind a Maizzle 5 -> 6 migration, not a dependency bump: Maizzle 6 drops the direct tailwindcss dependency in favour of @tailwindcss/postcss and @tailwindcss/vite ^4.3.0, which is the shape nswds-email-builder already runs (@maizzle/framework ^6.0.6 with tailwindcss ^4). Scoped by repository rather than fleet-wide because nswds-app, nswds-email and nswds-email-builder all legitimately run Tailwind 4. Owner has confirmed these two repos will NOT be migrated to Maizzle 6, so treat this block as permanent rather than pending. Note tailwindcss only became visible to Renovate here once it was declared to fix a phantom dependency (nswds-email-framework#217, nswds-email-starter#67); before that it was transitive and silently governed by Maizzle.

0.x minors are split out of the all-non-major group into their own PRs. Under SemVer a 0.x release carries no compatibility guarantee — 0.a.b -> 0.c.d may break freely — but Renovate still classifies that bump as `minor`, so `group:allNonMajor` batches it with genuinely safe updates. That is how @figma/rest-api-spec 0.33.0 -> 0.41.0 rode into nswds-tokens#130 behind 45 other bumps: 0.35.0 widened VariableValue to include null, `typeof null === 'object'` broke narrowing in compareVariableValues, and `npm run typecheck` failed — a review-time catch that a 400-line lockfile diff invites you to skim past. Ungrouping gives each 0.x minor its own PR, its own diff, and its own release notes to read. 0.x patches stay grouped: they remain bug-fix-only by convention and are the bulk of the volume.

Lint and format tooling automerges at minor as well as patch, in its own group. This is the other fleet-wide fan-out alongside the file sync: every release of @nswds/eslint-config or @nswds/prettier-config opens a PR in ~20 repos at once, and they are minors (1.1.0 -> 1.2.0), so the dev-patch rule below never catches them. The reason minor is safe *here specifically* and nowhere else is that these four packages are the only dependencies in the fleet whose entire effect is measured by required checks that already gate the merge: a formatting change from prettier or @nswds/prettier-config makes the committed tree fail `install / format` (prettier --check), and a rule change from eslint or @nswds/eslint-config fails `install / lint`. A bump that would change what the fleet does therefore cannot merge — it goes red and waits for a human, which is the same outcome as review, reached without 20 people-minutes of clicking. Scoped to devDependencies for the same reason as the dev-patch rule: config:recommended brings :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers, so devDeps commit chore(deps) and release nothing, while a prod dep would commit fix(deps) and publish unreviewed on the five npm repos. Majors are excluded and stay hand-reviewed — the eslint 10 block above is exactly why. Own group rather than riding in group:allNonMajor because automerge config merges across a group, which would hand automerge to every unrelated bump batched alongside. minimumReleaseAge and the rebaseWhen override carry the same rationale as the dev-patch rule: nobody reads an automerged PR, and 'conflicted' would strand one that falls behind main under strict required checks. Note the two in-house packages are not special-cased on age — a bad @nswds/eslint-config release should sit for three days like any other.

devDependency PATCH updates get their own group and automerge. Scope is deliberate on both axes. devDependencies only, because config:recommended pulls in :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers — Renovate commits production-dependency updates as `fix(deps)` and devDependencies as `chore(deps)`, and the shared release.config.mjs runs the conventionalcommits preset where `fix` cuts a patch release. Automerging a production patch would therefore publish to npm unreviewed on the five repos with @semantic-release/npm enabled (nswds-ui, nswds-tokens, nswds-app, nswds-eslint-config, nswds-prettier-config); `chore(deps)` releases nothing, so a devDependency patch lands on main and stops there. PATCH only, because patch is the one update type that is bug-fix-by-convention across both SemVer and the 0.x packages this fleet depends on. Own group rather than riding in group:allNonMajor, because automerge config merges across a group — leaving these in the all-non-major PR would hand automerge to every minor and every production bump batched alongside them. minimumReleaseAge holds each update until it is 3 days old: automerge means nobody reads these, so a release that is yanked or hot-patched within hours never becomes a merge. rebaseWhen is overridden to behind-base-branch because the top-level 'conflicted' would strand these — strict required status checks block a behind-but-clean branch from merging, and under 'conflicted' nothing would ever refresh it, so the PR would sit unmergeable forever. The bounded re-run cost that reintroduces is the point of the trade: these PRs are short-lived by construction, and the rebase leads to a merge rather than to another rebase. Everything else in the fleet keeps 'conflicted'.
